claims.text: Untreated MoNbTaW has conventional grain boundaries prone to embrittlement and localized deformation.
Minor Y doping combined with rapid solidification and low-temperature annealing induces thin amorphous grain-boundary complexions in MoNbTaW.
Annealing at approximately 700 °C for 1 hour promotes Y segregation to MoNbTaW grain boundaries.
Rapid solidification maintains a refined MoNbTaW microstructure.
Annealing at approximately 700 °C for 1 hour enables Y segregation without excessive grain growth.
The resulting amorphous or complexion films are enriched in Y.
Y segregation alters grain-boundary structure and energy.
Y-enriched grain-boundary complexions reduce interfacial embrittlement.
Y-enriched grain-boundary complexions facilitate grain-boundary sliding.
Reduced embrittlement and enhanced grain-boundary sliding delay crack initiation.
Delayed crack initiation permits more uniform plastic deformation.
Y doping and grain-boundary complexion formation leave the high-strength mechanisms in the grain interiors unaffected.
The proposed treatment preserves impact-induced energy release.
Relative to undoped MoNbTaW, the treated Y-doped alloy will have significantly improved tensile ductility.
Relative to undoped MoNbTaW, the treated Y-doped alloy will deform more uniformly across its microstructure.
The ductility and deformation improvements will occur with little or no loss of strength.
The ductility and deformation improvements will occur with little or no loss of impact reactivity.
Undoped MoNbTaW typically has limited ductility and nonuniform deformation leading to early failure despite high strength and impact-induced energy release.
Higher annealing temperatures or slower cooling rates may prevent formation of the desired grain-boundary complexion or cause grain growth.
